editorial:
Imagine your 11-year-old son suddenly turning into a nightmare. He isn't just acting out; he is swearing at everyone, vomiting on people, and making furniture fly across the room. You would be terrified, and that is exactly where this story starts. The parents try everything to fix him, but when nothing works, they call in Father Bowden. He is not your typical holy man. He is a WWII veteran struggling with bad memories and a drinking problem, which makes him a really interesting character to follow. The vibe is heavy and creepy, focusing on a battle between a broken man and a scary demon.

What really works here is the tension. The acting feels real, and the scenes where the boy loses control are genuinely unsettling. While it is a TV movie, it manages to feel more authentic than some big-budget horror films because it claims to be based on a true story. The pacing is solid, though some parts feel a bit slow. If you enjoy supernatural thrillers, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final act, Father Bowden performs a dangerous exorcism to save the boy. He has to face his own inner demons and guilt from the war to find the strength to fight the entity. After a huge struggle with screams and chaos, the demon is finally forced out of the child. The boy returns to normal, and Father Bowden finds a sense of peace and healing for his own troubled soul.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school exorcism movies and dark family dramas.
